response.close_all: Flatten every layer and stop trading for the week if any of these happen: (1) total floating NAV(-) across all layers exceeds 250 USD (10% of the 2,500 collateral); (2) BTC prints a 1d close below 79,000 or above 87,500, i.e. the range we are hunting in is broken; (3) a funding spike or exchange/liquidity event pushes BTC ATR14% above 4%; (4) end of the week review: close all layers in profit and any hostage older than 5 days that is within 1% of break-even. Otherwise layers are not closed in bulk; they are released one by one.
response.hostage_policy: A layer that goes against us is a hostage, not a loss. Rules: max 4 layers total across the whole watchlist, fixed ~625 USD notional each, never add size to a losing layer and never open a 5th layer. A hostage is held (NAV(-)) while the pair stays inside its weekly range; we use the next layer in a different symbol or at the opposite range edge to hunt small wins (+1.5-2.5%) and apply those wins to release the hostage at break-even or small profit. A hostage is surrendered only at its own fixed adverse-move limit (6-8% per symbol above) or at a 1d close outside the stated range, or when total NAV(-) hits the 250 USD close_all threshold. Realised profits (the 'captured hostages') are not reinvested into bigger layers this week; they stay as buffer. No revenge entries within 12h of a surrendered layer.
response.rationale: First week, no open RP and no history, so we start at 1x leverage (2,500 notional on 2,500 collateral), far below the 10x minimum max leverage on the watchlist, and we limit resources to 4 small layers. The market is a sideways, low-funding range: BTC is between its 1d swing low 79,732 and swing high 84,315, hugging weekly VWAP 82,109 with EMA20 above EMA50 but MACD histogram negative and shrinking; ETH, SOL and XRP show the same compressed structure with RSI in the mid-40s to high-50s. That is ideal for the hostage-hunt approach of collecting many small rotations at range edges rather than predicting direction. BTC and ETH get a two-sided bias because their edges are well defined; SOL gets a long-only bias because it sits on a 3-week base above EMA50 with the best risk/reward toward 108; XRP is two-sided inside 1.26-1.40. HYPE is excluded from trading because it is the weakest major (below VWAP, EMA20 under EMA50). Fixed-size layers, pre-set surrender distances and a hard 10% portfolio NAV(-) cap keep the main army alive so that mistakes can be repaired by the next layer instead of being cut immediately.
